fixed.what: The four Roussette de Savoie crus retagged advanced from master: the Codex's own Premier Cru bank asks them (a-tozwymby), so they are first asked from Premier Cru.
The key, Roussanne, was the longest option; the distractor Viognier became Mondeuse Blanche, and the explanation teaches all three distractors.
The key, Sixteen, was the longest option; the distractor Eleven became Fourteen.
The current Vin de Savoie text is now cited with its date, the order of 14 June 2023 published in BO-AGRI on 6 July 2023 (the ministry's official bulletin), which the author could not confirm.

confirmed: Roussette de Savoie: the order of 24 August 2021 (Journal officiel, 31 August 2021) exists as cited, Altesse alone, still white only, and the four crus Frangy (Chaumont, Desingy, Frangy), Marestel (Jongieux, Lucey), Monterminod (Saint-Alban-Leysse) and Monthoux (Saint-Jean-de-Chevelu).
Château-Chalon: four communes, Château-Chalon, Domblans, Ménétru-le-Vignoble and Nevy-sur-Seille, Domblans only in part (the text in opposition from February 2026 limits it to part of its territory).
Arbin and Saint-Jean-de-la-Porte are Mondeuse reds; Saint-Jeoire-Prieuré is a white cru; sixteen Vin de Savoie crus, as the Codex's Premier Cru bank and the interprofession give it.
open: A new Macvin du Jura or Marc du Jura text was homologated on 1 December 2025 (the search could not show which, nor its content); nothing the article claims (unfermented must and Jura marc, three colours, AOC 1991) is known to change, and no change is claimed.
One encyclopaedia counts seventeen Vin de Savoie geographic names; sixteen stands as the interprofession's and the Codex's figure.
